subject: Transport adapter selection for EdgeForge private deploy - peering vs PrivateLink vs IPSec
messages:
From: Danielle Park <dpark@edgeforge.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeForge NetOps <netops@edgeforge.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy connectivity - initial ask

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're starting planning for the EdgeForge private deployment and need to pick a primary transport strategy from these three: VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), or site-to-site IPSec VPN. Our top concerns are:
- Least privilege surface for regulated data flows (we're in PCI scope)
- Predictable tail latency for inference (95th/99th percentile)
- Operational simplicity for our infra team (limited SRE headcount)
- Cost sensitivity — we'd prefer predictable monthly cost vs variable egress spikes

I've attached our current network diagram and a short list of constraints. Could you outline what you typically recommend and any hard blockers for each option? Also, do you have a checklist for PrivateLink onboarding?

Appreciate it,
Danielle Park
Director, Cloud Engineering
EdgeForge

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deploy connectivity - initial ask

Thanks Danielle — good, concise constraints. High-level summary up front: all three are viable but tradeoffs cluster around security surface, latency predictability, and ops overhead.

Quick lay-of-the-land:
- VPC peering: lowest-latency (no extra gateways), but requires full-route exposure between VPCs and can complicate multi-account routing and cross-region setups. Good if you need <10ms p95 and can manage routing/security groups.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): best for minimizing data-plane surface (Redwood exposes endpoints; you keep minimal ingress surface). Slightly higher p95 due to NAT/ENI hops but very strong for PCI/zero-trust requirements because you avoid broad VPC routing. It can be more operational work up-front (ENI quotas, endpoint services) but simpler long-term.
- Site-to-site IPSec VPN: flexible for on-prem or non-cloud edge sites, easier to reason about billing (fixed appliance cost + tunnels) but typically higher and more variable latency and lower throughput. Good as fallback/burst path.

Kimberly — can you add a brief technical checklist / blockers for PrivateLink (quotas, TLS certs, health checks)? Ben — I suspect there's a pricing note about sustained egress vs per-connection interface costs you should call out.

Proposal: schedule a 45-minute alignment call Wed or Thu this week, then we'll produce a 1-page recommendation with action items (certificates, IAM role bindings, required endpoint quotas).

Cheers,
Mateo
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Danielle / team — adding concrete operational checks for PrivateLink and a short matrix for the three options. See inline.

PrivateLink checklist (high-priority items):
- ENI quota: confirm account ENI limits in target regions and request increases early (2–3 business days typical).
- Security policy: create IAM role for endpoint service registration; plan for mutual TLS or signed JWT verify depending on your gateway.
- Internal DNS: configure VPC resolver rules to point the service FQNs at interface endpoint IPs; document TTL and failover behavior.
- Health checks: Redwood expects a 200 on /healthz and will include a cert for TLS; make sure your NACLs and SGs permit the health probes.
- Logging/Audit: ensure Flow Logs are enabled for subnets with ENIs and push to your SIEM (we can ingest logs via our observability connectors).
- Maintenance window: plan 2x 1-hour windows for ENI replacements/endpoint service updates.

Tradeoff matrix (summary):
- Latency: Peering < PrivateLink < IPSec VPN (median difference ~2–8ms typical; see attached latency matrix CSV).
- Security surface: PrivateLink (narrowest) > IPSec (tunneled but broad depending on routing) > Peering (broad VPC route table exposure).
- Ops: Peering (low infra config) vs PrivateLink (moderate initial quota/setup) vs IPSec (ongoing tunnel ops).
- Multi-region: Peering is awkward cross-region without transit; PrivateLink can be regional with replication; IPSec works across on-prem to cloud.

Blockers: interface endpoints require you to accept per-ENI costs and possibly adjust private DNS — not a blocker but a procurement ask. Also if you need source IP preservation for strict IP-based allowlists, peering preserves source IPs best; PrivateLink NATs to ENI IPs which can complicate audit logs unless you forward original client identity.

Attachment: peering-vs-ipsec-latency-matrix.csv (sample 95/99 latency measurements)

Happy to walk through diagrams on the call.

—Kimberly

Quick answers and proposed next steps: 

1) Compliance: yes — for PCI and narrow-datapath compliance we typically recommend PrivateLink as first choice. It reduces blast radius and simplifies compliance attestations because the service uses endpoint NLB/ENI rather than broad VPC routing. We'll include a compliance playbook excerpt in the follow-up doc.

2) Source IP: PrivateLink does NAT to the endpoint ENI IPs, so if you require source-IP preservation for forensic logs, two approaches:
   a) Keep peering for the subset of traffic where source-IP matters (hybrid approach).
   b) Have Redwood add an X-Forwarded-For style header at the application layer and send requestor identity in the request metadata (requires mutual agreement for audit chains).

3) Cost: Ben will follow up with a ballpark. My quick rule-of-thumb: PrivateLink has per-ENI hourly costs + data processing; peering is free but egress charges still apply depending on cloud provider. For your projected baseline we expect PrivateLink to be modestly higher (5–20% depending on region and ENI counts) but more predictable from a security standpoint.

Next steps:
- Ben: produce a short monthly cost delta estimate and note any required committed tiers we should suggest.
- Kimberly: I'll sync with you to flesh out the PrivateLink operational runbook (ENI quotas, DNS changes, health-check SLA).
- Danielle / EdgeForge: after you upload the updated diagram we'll schedule the alignment call — suggest Fri 11am or Mon 9am PT.

I'll draft the 1-page recommendation after the call and include a suggested hybrid fallback (Primary: PrivateLink; Fallback: IPSec tunnels for multi-region/on-prem edges).

Cheers,
Mateo
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
